Do you remember the first time you backed the car out of the driveway yourself? That feeling was pure freedom. But for your parents, that moment was likely one of the most terrifying of their lives. When you were a teenager, they had absolutely no way of knowing how fast you were driving, where you had gone, when you would arrive, or how safely you were behind the wheel. "No news is good news" — until you checked in, hope was the only tool they had.

If you currently have a teenager who drives, count yourself lucky that you no longer have to live in that age of worry. Although 2026 technology has plenty of drawbacks, HeyPolo is clearly an example of technology that makes teenage driving safer and life better.

HeyPolo is more than just an upgraded version of Apple's "Find My" service

HeyPolo is a family safety app that bundles real-time location sharing, arrival and departure notifications, SOS emergency alerts, and driving safety features all into one price. The driving features are what set it apart from typical location-sharing apps (such as "Find My"). Every single time your child gets behind the wheel, they are tracked and scored, so you can clearly see how they are performing: how fast they are going, whether they are using their smartphone while driving, whether there is any hard braking or sudden acceleration, and whether any serious driving incidents have been detected.

The "Driving Score" rates each trip based on their actual driving behaviour, so you no longer have to guess whether your teenager is really driving safely. You can see the data, have a serious conversation if the performance is poor, and as their driving habits improve, the score goes up over time. Compared with anything the previous generation had access to, this is far more useful for helping new licence-holders improve.

Crash detection, arrival notifications, and more

HeyPolo can detect a crash and automatically notify you. Combined with arrival notifications — whether your child arrives at school, practice, a friend's house, or back home, a trigger is sent — you move from "hoping no news is good news" to actually knowing whether they are safe. You don't have to wait for them to text or call you once they arrive; you can know exactly when they got there, and that peace of mind is priceless for a parent. HeyPolo updates location every 5 seconds, so your location information is always accurate.

One price, shared by the whole family

A single HeyPolo subscription already covers your entire family, with absolutely no extra per-person fees. It works on both iPhone and Android, so families with a mix of devices don't need to worry. HeyPolo is developed by the team behind Surfshark, so it has a solid privacy infrastructure. They don't sell your data, you decide what to share, with whom, and when to stop sharing, and all data is automatically deleted every 7 days. For a location-based app, this is essential when it comes to privacy.

HeyPolo offers a 30-day money-back guarantee with no contracts of any kind — there is simply no reason not to give it a try.
